lede: The CIFAR run grows from 4×4 to 32×32. Logged sample std falls from 0.58 to 0.10, and the last grid is one gray field.
title: Progressive GAN on CIFAR-10
question: Does growing the resolution from 4×4 to 32×32 stabilize CIFAR-10 samples?
process: `GrowingGenerator` and `GrowingDiscriminator` in `src/mnist_pg_gan/model.py` add resolution on the schedule from `_phases`: stable \(4\times 4\), then a fade and a stable phase at 8, 16, and 32. During a fade, `_blend` sets \( \alpha = (\mathrm{epoch\ in\ phase}+1)/\mathrm{epochs} \). The run is CIFAR-10, 200 train and 40 test images per class, two epochs per phase, 14 epochs. `growth.json` and `growth_timeline.png` record every phase. The chart is logged sample std of the fixed noise batch. `mode_collapse` is sample std under 0.2 times real std.

opening.summary: The growth archive is on disk: growth.json, the timeline, and a frame for every epoch. Color blocks at 4×4 become finer noise, then a shared gray field at 32×32. Logged sample std falls from 0.581 to 0.104 along that path.

marks.summary: Epoch 14 is 32×32 stable. Logged sample std is 0.104. The scored grid has sample std 0.1040 against real std 0.493, a ratio of 0.211. mode_collapse stays false because the cutoff is 0.20. The picture is one gray-purple field repeated across the batch. Eval D on the log is 1.520 and eval G is 0.700. Two epochs at 32×32 was enough for the samples to agree with each other and not enough to grow an object.
marks.hover: epoch 14 · 32×32 stable · scored ratio 0.211 · flag false

reflection.worked: The schedule ran all seven phases and wrote the timeline the notebook reads. Epoch 6, the bold point, is the last resolution where the fixed-noise batch is still a set of different color fields. Discriminator and generator losses stay in a band around 1 through the early phases.
reflection.unexpected: Resolution growth and sample variety move in opposite directions. By 32×32 every cell is the same gray field. The collapse flag stays false because 0.104 / 0.493 = 0.211, just above the 0.2 cutoff.
reflection.why: Each new resolution gets two epochs on 2,000 images. That is enough for the generator to find one average color that survives the discriminator, and not enough to fit airplanes and trucks. The fade spends one of those two epochs at a half-blended block. A short stay at 32×32 favors the mean image.
reflection.improve: Give the 16×16 and 32×32 stable phases more epochs before judging CIFAR, and plot the spread ratio against the 0.2 line so a batch of identical gray squares cannot sit just outside the flag. The timeline is already the right picture to watch while that longer run goes.
